label: Outstanding AfCFTA rules-of-origin annexes for the contested sectors are completed before mid-2027
basis: Rules of origin for the sectors where regional value chains are genuinely contested — autos and textiles above all — require agreement among State Parties, and the negotiation has already run well past its original target without closing those annexes. Reference class: multilateral technical annexes whose economics are zero-sum between members, which close slowly or not at all.
rationale: A MARKER priced well below even money, and logged precisely because it is a negative. The asymmetry is structural: a trade agreement's tariff schedule can run on autopilot while the rules that determine WHICH goods qualify stay open, and the open rules are the binding constraint on actual trade. SOFT part: all of it — this is a negotiation among sovereigns and therefore the discretionary-choice class the engine is worst at, which is exactly why it is stated at 0.35 rather than dressed as an invariant.
market: Without rules of origin, a tariff schedule does not move a single container; this is the gate on the whole AfCFTA trade.

label: Disbursements under upper-credit-tranche IMF arrangements remain conditioned on board completion of a scheduled review, not on calendar time
basis: PROGRAM-DOCUMENT STRUCTURE: every extended or credit-facility arrangement is approved with a schedule of reviews, each tied to performance criteria assessed at a named test date, and the associated tranche becomes available only when the Executive Board completes that review. The conditionality architecture is institutional, written into the arrangement itself, and identical in form across countries.
rationale: An institutional invariant about the MECHANISM, which is why it can be stated without naming a country or a date — and that is deliberate, because naming a specific review board date I was not certain of would be inventing a fact. Its value is as the correction for the commonest frontier error: treating a program as a funding stream when it is a sequence of conditional gates. SOFT part: waivers of non-observance, rephasings and augmentations are all available and routinely granted, so a missed target is not a stopped program.
market: Program money is gated, not scheduled; frontier curves that price it as an annuity are wrong.

label: No Common Framework bondholder exchange completes before an official-creditor understanding is in place
basis: PROCESS SEQUENCE: the Common Framework requires an IMF-supported program, an official creditor committee, and comparability of treatment between official and private claims. Comparability cannot be assessed against an official envelope that does not yet exist, so the official step is a logical precondition to the private one. The constraint is the ORDER of the steps, which is institutional, not the willingness of any participant.
rationale: A sequence invariant — the shape that makes 'when will the restructuring finish?' tractable without forecasting any creditor's behaviour. You cannot run the legs in parallel, so the total duration is at least the sum of the slowest path, and that is arithmetic. SOFT part: sovereigns have launched consent solicitations and reprofiling exchanges OUTSIDE the Common Framework entirely, which would satisfy a loose reading of 'bondholder exchange' while leaving this node's premise intact — the resolution source must specify a Common Framework case.
market: Sequence, not goodwill, is what sets the duration of a frontier workout and therefore its recovery discount rate.

label: Official 2026 population figure shows another y/y decline
basis: Demographic arithmetic: the birth cohort and the death cohort are both largely determined years in advance. A reversal would require a fertility jump with no precedent.
rationale: INVARIANT — pure demographic arithmetic, and one of the few things in this tree that is genuinely close to certain. This is the row class the book scores 0.10 Brier on.
market: Demography is the slow denominator under every China demand row.

label: Headline budget deficit ratio set at or above 3.5%
basis: Base rate off the recent trajectory of widening headline ratios; still a discretionary budget decision, so capped.
rationale: Scheduled-print class for a discretionary number. The engine's edge is in knowing WHEN it lands, not what it will be - which is why the date is near-certain and the value is capped. The LGSB quota row below is the better read on the actual impulse and the two are one view.
market: The headline ratio understates the real impulse; the LGSB quota row below matters more.

label: 2027 growth target set at 'around 5%'
basis: Strong base rate: the target has been set at or around 5% repeatedly, and the target is a political constant more than an economic forecast. Reference class: the last several NPCs.
rationale: Scheduled with a strong institutional base rate. Note it is still a CHOICE, which caps it under the invariant rows; 0.72 sits at the top of what R13 allows only because the reference class is this tight.
market: The target is the fiscal constraint, not a forecast.

label: Local government special bond quota set above CNY 4 trillion
basis: Base rate off the recent quota path; a discretionary number on a fixed calendar.
rationale: Scheduled. The LGSB quota is the real fiscal impulse and a better row than the headline deficit — noted so the two are not treated as independent.
market: The quota is the actual construction-demand number.

label: USDCNY fixes inside 6.80-7.60 on every fixing through Q2 2027
basis: The fix is a managed, published daily number with a demonstrated tolerance band. This is closer to an institutional invariant than a market level.
rationale: Level row on a MANAGED price — which makes it institutional rather than discretionary. The distinction matters: the band is defended by policy, so the constraint is real.

no_view.note: ASSUMED spot fix 7.15 and 0.15%/day FIX vol (~2.4% annualised). The row is about the PBoC's daily FIX, which is managed and far less volatile than spot; 192 sessions to 6/30/27.

market: A break of the band is the single loudest signal China has stopped defending stability.

label: PBoC cuts the reserve requirement ratio at least once by mid-2027
basis: Capped 0.55: a central-bank discretionary action, the #26 class. The base rate of at least one RRR cut in a three-quarter window is high historically, which is precisely why the cap matters — the temptation is to price it 0.80.
rationale: DIRECTION + discretionary committee. This row exists partly as a live test of the cap: the base rate genuinely argues higher, and the rule says no. If a run of these resolves HIT at 0.55, that is evidence to relax R13 deliberately rather than by accident.
market: RRR cuts are liquidity, not demand; the transmission is the question.

label: PBoC reports gold reserve additions in at least 8 of the next 12 monthly reports
basis: Marker on a monthly published series with a long established run. Persistence, not turn.
rationale: Marker class: the claim is that an observable keeps APPEARING, not that it rises or falls. Cheap to check monthly, which is what lesson 6 asks for. Note this is a persistence row on official-sector behaviour, so its failure mode is a policy change, not a price move.
market: Official-sector buying is the structural bid under the gold row in commodities-metals.

label: A Lower Basin shortage condition is declared for calendar 2027
basis: RULE-TRIGGERED: the shortage tier is set by a published projection of Lake Mead elevation on a fixed date under an existing operating agreement. Given current elevations, the trigger is close to arithmetic.
rationale: The best example in this buildout of a hidden invariant: this looks like a hydrology forecast and is actually a threshold rule applied to a measurement. Find more of these.
market: Water allocation is a hard input to agriculture and to southwestern power.

label: Global insured natural catastrophe losses for 2026 are reported above $100bn
basis: Base rate: the $100bn threshold has been exceeded in most recent years, and most of the year's events have already occurred by the time this is logged.
rationale: Invariant-adjacent because the year is nearly complete - most of the outcome is already determined and merely unreported. A retrospective-arithmetic row.
market: Insured losses are the price signal that transmits physical risk into capital costs.

label: California statewide snowpack peaks below 110% of average in 2027
basis: Measured on a fixed survey calendar; the base rate of a below-110% peak is comfortably above even across the historical record.
rationale: Scheduled measurement with a base-rate value and a NAMED survey as the resolution source. Naming the survey is the #59 fix: that row was scored against the engine only because nobody had written down which measurement counted.
market: Snowpack is the hydro and agricultural input for the whole western US.

label: US crop insurance indemnities for 2026 are reported above $10bn
basis: Retrospective arithmetic: the crop year is essentially complete, so this is a reporting-lag row rather than a forecast.
rationale: Retrospective-arithmetic class, same as the insured-loss row. Rows about facts that have already happened but have not yet been published are systematically under-used.
market: Indemnities are the fiscal transmission of physical risk into the farm economy.

label: At least one European country issues a heat-related power or water restriction in summer 2027
basis: Marker with a strong recent base rate driven by nuclear cooling constraints and hydro levels — both physical.
rationale: Marker with a physical mechanism (thermal plant cooling limits), not a temperature forecast. The restriction is triggered by measured river temperature, another rule-triggered invariant.
market: Cooling constraints are why a European heatwave is a power-price event.

label: Platinum records a supply deficit for 2026
basis: South African shaft depletion and power constraints cap supply; the constraint is physical and already visible in reported output.
rationale: Invariant. Correlated with the silver row through 'precious industrial deficit' - declared so the book does not treat them as two independent confirmations (#70/#27).
market: PGMs are the most supply-constrained precious complex.

label: Silver records another annual structural deficit for 2026
basis: Industrial demand (solar, electronics) is contracted and growing while mine supply is byproduct-constrained - silver supply cannot respond to price because it is mined as a byproduct of copper, lead and zinc.
rationale: Invariant with a genuinely elegant mechanism: byproduct supply is price-INELASTIC by construction. That is a physical constraint, not a market view.
market: The byproduct constraint is why silver behaves like an industrial metal with a monetary tail.

label: World wheat stocks-to-use for 2026/27 is reported below 32%
basis: Scheduled monthly WASDE-style reporting; the value depends on harvests that are partly unknown. Priced near even because it genuinely is.
rationale: Another honestly near-even row. #39's food-emergency leg failed partly because the engine wanted a dramatic number; the undramatic answer is that stocks-to-use is a coin near its threshold.
market: Stocks-to-use is the only grain number that maps to price non-linearly.

label: NOAA declares an ENSO-neutral or La Nina state for the 2027 northern summer
basis: Scheduled official declaration on a fixed monthly cycle; the base rate of neutral-or-Nina against El Nino across a randomly chosen season favours this side.
rationale: Scheduled EVENT with a base-rate value. The declaration is by a named agency on a fixed calendar, which makes the resolution source unambiguous - the #59 fix.
market: ENSO state is the single biggest exogenous input to the ag complex.

label: Aggregate reported backlog at the top five US primes sets a record at the next annual reporting
basis: Arithmetic on signed contracts: backlog rises when bookings exceed revenue, and the book-to-bill has been above one on a war footing with European budgets enacted.
rationale: INVARIANT - backlog is an audited number about contracts already signed. This is the correct replacement for the #3 style of defence row.
market: Record backlog with flat deliveries is the throughput problem, not a demand problem.

label: Japan's enacted FY2027 defence budget exceeds its FY2026 level in nominal terms
basis: Multi-year build-up plan already legislated with an annual path; the nominal comparison is arithmetic against a legislated baseline.
rationale: Invariant via a legislated multi-year path - the same structure as the German fiscal row. Legislated paths are the most reliable political objects available.
market: Japanese procurement is the second-largest new demand pool after Europe.

label: At least 24 NATO members are reported at or above 2% of GDP for 2026
basis: Enacted budgets for the reporting year; this is a count of decisions already taken, published on a fixed annual cycle.
rationale: Invariant. Correlated with the europe lane's defence row - the same enacted budgets counted against a different threshold. Declared, not double-counted.
market: The count is the demand signal European primes book against.

label: US working gas in storage ends the injection season above the five-year average
basis: Weekly EIA series with a hard seasonal endpoint. Priced near even: LNG export pull against record production is genuinely balanced, and pretending otherwise is false precision.
rationale: A deliberately near-even row. The book's measured resolution is ~0.00 partly because everything was stated between 0.40 and 0.88 — a row that is honestly 0.58 should be logged at 0.58 and not talked up into a story.
market: Storage is the winter risk premium in one number.

label: OPEC+ leaves headline quotas unchanged at the November meeting
basis: Hard cap 0.55: this is a cartel of sovereigns exercising discretion. #29 priced exactly this shape at 0.58 on a premise that had already evaporated and scored 0.34.
rationale: DIRECTION + discretionary. Capped at the ceiling and left there. The lesson from #29 is not 'predict OPEC better', it is 'OPEC is not a mechanism'.
market: Unchanged is the low-vol outcome for the band row below.

label: Brent front-month trades inside $85-$125 for the whole of Q4
basis: No-view odds from `range_odds.py --spot 98 --lo 85 --hi 125 --days 70 --vol 2.5` = 0.33 (--vol is DAILY PERCENT; 2.5%/day is ~40% annualised, consistent with realised wartime Brent). Priced AT the no-view number with no divergence claimed.
rationale: [9/22 CORRECTION #2 - the first correction was WRONG] On 9/21 this was logged at 0.66 without running range_odds.py at all. On 9/22 it was 'corrected' UP to 0.82 on a run that passed --vol 0.80, and --vol is DAILY PERCENT, not annualised: 0.80%/day is ~13% annualised, roughly a third of what wartime Brent has actually realised (101-109 since 9/9, peak close 108.75). At an honest 2.5%/day (~40% annualised), `range_odds.py --spot 98 --lo 85 --hi 125 --days 70 --vol 2.5` returns NO-VIEW 0.33, with only 0.68 sigma to the lower bound. So the original 0.66 was ALREADY too high, and the 0.82 'fix' moved it further the wrong way. Repriced to 0.35, at the no-view number, with NO divergence claimed - the only dated catalyst in sight (the 9/22 Hormuz reopening report) pushes the LOWER bound, not the upper. A units error inside a correction is exactly the shape of the VIX-lookahead and rolling-window failures: the arithmetic was never wrong, the input was. || Level row, ONE asset, explicit band, wide. Note what it is NOT: a call on whether oil goes up or down. The book is 0-for-8 on that question in this tape.

no_view.note: Spot 103.87 is the repo's own tape (STATE.md 9/20). Vol 2.5%/day ~ 40% annualised, which is what the repo's own 9/9-9/20 Brent record implies (101-109 range, peak close 108.75) - a war-premium crude regime, NOT the 0.8%/day (12.8% annualised) that Brent has never sustained. 65 Q4 sessions.

market: The band is the tradeable object; the direction is not.

label: ULSD crack stays above $25/bbl on every weekly close to 3/2027
basis: Duration. Distillate is structurally short on closed conversion capacity plus a rerouting premium; the floor holds unless demand breaks.
rationale: Duration + a physical capacity constraint. Note this is the SAME view as the refinery row and is therefore not independent evidence for it — flagged here so the book does not count one thesis twice (the #70/#27 error).

no_view.note: ASSUMED: the >$25 ULSD crack regime is ~200d old; median length of a wide-distillate-crack regime ~400d (crack regimes are shorter-lived than rig-count regimes).

market: Diesel is the industrial read and the pass-through channel into core goods.

label: US oil rig count stays above 400 every week through Q1 2027
basis: Duration framing. With crude above $100 the drilling economics are not the binding constraint; a fall through 400 would require a price collapse first. Weekly published.
rationale: [9/22 CORRECTION] cycle_odds.py puts the no-view survival band at 0.87-0.89 and this row was logged at 0.76, more than 0.10 outside it with no dated catalyst in the basis; re-priced 0.76 -> 0.80 into the band. Duration re-expression of what would otherwise be a shale-response direction call. The conditional structure (only breaks if price breaks first) makes it a near-invariant.

no_view.note: ASSUMED: the rig count has been above 400 for ~400d; median length of an above-400 spell ~900d.

market: Rig counts are the slow supply response; they are a lagging confirmation, never a signal.

label: A previously announced refinery closure completes on schedule
basis: Capital already committed: an announced closure is a capital decision taken, and reversal requires fresh capital plus a restart schedule once units are cold. Reference class: announced refinery closures that completed.
rationale: Invariant class: a closure announcement is a committed action, unlike a strike PLAN (#72), which is a negotiating instrument. The distinction between committed and announced-intent is the single most useful line the 16.14 patch drew.
market: Closures are why crack spreads can stay wide with crude flat.

label: US summer 2027 peak load sets a record
basis: Near-arithmetic on the demand side: datacenter load additions are contracted years ahead and electrification is monotonic. The residual risk is weather, not demand.
rationale: Invariant-adjacent: contracted load is capital-committed. The only real uncertainty is a cool summer, which is a stated, bounded risk rather than a narrative.
market: Load growth is the physical fact under every AI-power trade in the markets-ai lane.

label: ECB leaves the deposit rate unchanged in December
basis: Capped 0.55 — committee discretion, the #26 class. An energy shock cuts both ways for the ECB (inflationary and contractionary), so there is no mechanism argument for divergence.
rationale: DIRECTION + committee. Note the internal-consistency requirement: this book already says the Fed hiked into the same oil shock. If this row were priced as a confident hold, the book would be claiming the same shock means opposite things at two central banks without saying why. It might — but it has to SAY why.
market: ECB-Fed divergence is the euro trade.

label: German federal investment spending in the 2027 budget exceeds the 2025 level in nominal terms
basis: Nominal comparison against an already-legislated expansion; the base-effect identity makes this arithmetic rather than a policy forecast.
rationale: Invariant, and an explicit use of doctrine 13d.2 the right way round: a NOMINAL comparison against a legislated baseline is arithmetic. The twice-repeated y/y miss came from doing this backwards.
market: German investment is the only large European fiscal impulse in the window.

label: France's reported deficit for 2026 exceeds 4.5% of GDP
basis: Fiscal outturns are largely determined by the time three quarters have elapsed; the reporting date is a fixed Eurostat cycle.
rationale: Scheduled with an arithmetic core — most of the year is already spent. This is the 'scheduled print backed by arithmetic' class at 12-for-14.
market: The French deficit is the OAT spread and therefore the EU fiscal-rules fight.

label: EU gas storage ends the 2026-27 withdrawal season above 25% full
basis: Published daily; the endpoint is seasonal and the outcome is dominated by weather plus LNG availability, both partially observable in advance.
rationale: Scheduled with a physical core. Explicitly dependent on the LNG row in energy-supply — the dependency is declared rather than double-counted.
market: Storage exit level sets the summer refill bid and next winter's European premium.

label: At least 20 NATO members report defence spending at or above 2% of GDP for 2026
basis: Budgets for the reporting year are already enacted; this is a count of decisions already taken, reported on a fixed annual cycle.
rationale: INVARIANT: enacted budgets are capital-committed. Contrast with a row about future pledges, which would be rhetoric (doctrine 12.1 / R03).
market: Enacted European defence budgets are the demand under the defense-industrial lane.

label: EURUSD trades inside 0.95-1.20 on every close through Q2 2027
basis: Wide band, no-view odds. A 25-figure range on the most liquid cross over three quarters is a high-probability containment claim, not a view.
rationale: Deliberately a BAND and deliberately wide — the anti-#69 construction. One asset, two bounds, wide enough that it is a genuine claim about volatility rather than direction.

no_view.note: ASSUMED spot 1.08 and 0.50%/day (~8% annualised, EURUSD's usual range). 192 sessions to 6/30/27.

market: The cross is where Fed-ECB divergence actually prints.

label: BTP-Bund 10y spread stays under 250bp on every close to mid-2027
basis: Level row with an institutional backstop (the ECB's transmission instrument) that has never been tested to failure. Priced off distance-to-threshold.
rationale: [9/22 CORRECTION] range_odds.py puts the no-view odds at 0.99 and this row was logged at 0.76, -0.23 off it with no dated catalyst in the basis; re-priced 0.76 -> 0.82 toward the arithmetic. Level, one spread, one side. The backstop is an institutional invariant; the spread is a market price. Naming which part is which is what keeps the row honest.

no_view.note: ASSUMED spot 105bp BTP-Bund and 2.5%/day relative vol (~2-3bp/day on 105bp). 192 sessions.

market: The periphery spread is the European version of the credit rows in rates-credit.

label: UK 30y gilt yield prints above 6.00% on any close by mid-2027
basis: Marker on a tail event. Priced BELOW the book's average on purpose: a book whose rows all sit between 0.40 and 0.88 has no resolution, and genuine tails must be logged as tails.
rationale: A deliberately LOW-probability row. The 9/20 research found every row stated between 0.40 and 0.88 and small-sample-corrected resolution near zero. You cannot fix that by lowering high rows; you fix it by being willing to say 'probably not' and be right.
market: A gilt event is the fastest route from a fiscal story to a global rates event.

label: The December SEP median shows at least one further 2027 hike
basis: Scheduled publication of a committee median - a discretionary aggregate. STATE.md already carries a 0.60 on a second hike by 12/9; this row is the SEP expression of the same view and is therefore NOT independent of it.
rationale: Scheduled-print class for a discretionary value, capped. Critically: this row and STATE.md's 'fomc-oct second hike 0.60' are ONE view, and saying so is the lesson-7 discipline the book has never enforced. Two rows on one view is a hedge, not two insights.
market: The dot path, not the meeting, is what the curve actually prices.

label: The 2027 FOMC voter rotation proceeds by statutory schedule
basis: The rotation of Reserve Bank presidents among voting seats is fixed by statute and schedule.
rationale: INVARIANT: statutory rotation. Included because voter composition is a real input to the dissent-count mechanism that doctrine 11a now uses to price hikes - and it is knowable with certainty a year ahead.
market: Who votes is knowable; how they vote is not. Price only the knowable half.

label: Core PCE y/y prints inside 2.5-4.0% on every release through Q2 2027
basis: Band on a slow-moving y/y series; the base-effect path is arithmetic and the energy pass-through has a known lag length (13g).
rationale: [9/22 CORRECTION] range_odds.py puts the no-view odds at 1.00 and this row was logged at 0.70, -0.30 off it with no dated catalyst in the basis; re-priced 0.70 -> 0.82 toward the arithmetic. Level with a wide band and an explicit base-effect computation. Note 13g: do not downgrade the pass-through thesis on less than one lag length of tape - that error cost #76.

no_view.note: ASSUMED spot core PCE 3.1% y/y and 2.0%/MONTH relative vol (~0.06pp - a y/y series moves slowly by construction). One period = one monthly release; 9 releases to Q2 2027.

market: Core PCE is the mandate variable; everything else is commentary.

label: The 10y TIPS real yield stays above 1.50% on every close through Q2 2027
basis: No-view odds off the distance to the threshold on a published daily series. With the policy rate raised and breakevens contained, a fall through 1.50 requires either a growth scare or a dovish turn - both identifiable in advance and both named as the falsifiers.
rationale: Level with the two falsifying mechanisms named up front. A row that says what would break it is a pre-registered falsifier, which is lesson 1.

no_view.note: ASSUMED spot 10y TIPS real yield 2.30% and 1.5%/day relative vol. 192 sessions to 6/30/27.

market: The real rate is the actual discount rate under every equity row in this tree.

label: Nigerian presidential ballot falls inside the statutory 150-to-30-day pre-expiry window
basis: STATUTORY WINDOW, NOT A SCHEDULED DATE: the constitution and the Electoral Act require the presidential election to be held not earlier than 150 days and not later than 30 days before the expiry of the incumbent term, and require the commission to publish a notice of election ahead of the poll. The claim is about the WINDOW, which is statutory arithmetic; the exact polling day is set by the commission inside it and is not asserted here.
rationale: Written this way on purpose. I do not know Nigeria's 2027 polling date and will not guess one, so the node turns on the statutory bracket rather than on a day. That is the `npt-notice` move: a bill tabled is not a notice filed, and a commission timetable announced is not a statutory window changed. SOFT part: the commission's choice inside the window, and the real possibility that litigation reruns individual contests after the presidential poll.
market: The window, not the day, is what bounds pre-election naira and fuel-subsidy positioning.

label: French presidential first round falls inside the Article 7 twenty-to-thirty-five-day pre-expiry window
basis: CONSTITUTIONAL WINDOW: Article 7 of the Fifth Republic constitution requires the election of the President to be held not fewer than twenty and not more than thirty-five days before the expiry of the incumbent's powers, with the second round fourteen days after the first. The government fixes the actual Sundays by decree inside that bracket, so the window is constitutional arithmetic and the day is executive.
rationale: Deliberately a window row: I am not certain of the decreed 2027 Sundays and will not state one as fact. Article 7 also supplies the two-round interval, which means the resolving date for a presidential contest is mechanically fourteen days after whatever first round is decreed. SOFT part: Article 7 also covers vacancy, in which case the window is recomputed off the vacancy rather than off the term, and the node would need re-dating rather than resolving.
market: A fixed fourteen-day inter-round gap is the cleanest dated OAT and CAC vol structure in Europe.

label: Kenyan general election on the second Tuesday of August 2027 (2027-08-10)
basis: CONSTITUTIONAL TEXT: the 2010 Constitution fixes the general election for the second Tuesday in August in every fifth year. Applying the formula to August 2027 gives the 10th (computed). The date is in the constitution, not in an electoral statute, so moving it needs a constitutional amendment rather than a commission decision.
rationale: A constitution that literally names a weekday-of-month is the best possible basis for an election-date row. SOFT part: Kenya's courts have twice had to order reruns or extend timetables, so the general election DAY has held while the resolution of the contest has slipped past it; a node dated on the first ballot must not be read as a node on the final declaration. No view on the contest.
market: The August date frames Kenyan eurobond and shilling risk a full year ahead.

label: Second-round Medicare negotiated prices take effect on the statutory date
basis: The effective date is written into statute and the selected-drug list is already published. Residual risk is litigation, which is a separate row.
rationale: INVARIANT: a statutory effective date plus an already-published selected-drug list. The litigation risk is split into its own node rather than bundled in, because a row that needs BOTH the date to hold AND the courts to stay out is a conjunction, and conjunctions are where #63 and #39 died.
market: Negotiated prices are a direct, dated hit to a known set of revenue lines.

label: No GLP-1 product appears on the FDA drug shortage list on 2027-06-30
basis: Marker on a published list. Capacity additions are capital-committed and commissioning; demand growth is the offsetting unknown.
rationale: Marker with a named, published resolution source. Two capital-committed forces in opposition again, so the honest price is mid.
market: Shortage status is the cleanest single read on whether capacity has caught demand.

label: Electoral roll revision continues on its published cycle with the statutory qualifying dates through 2027
basis: STATUTORY CYCLE: the Representation of the People Act, as amended, provides multiple qualifying dates per year for enrolment rather than a single January 1 cut-off, and the Election Commission conducts a special summary revision on a published schedule with draft publication, a claims-and-objections window and final publication. Each stage has a notified date; the cycle is a statutory administrative process.
rationale: Scheduled class on an administrative calendar, included because roll revision is the upstream constraint on every electoral timetable in the lane — a commission cannot notify a poll against a roll that has not been finally published. SOFT part: intensive or special revisions ordered ahead of a state election run on bespoke schedules that override the annual cycle, and those are discretionary; so the node is about the ORDINARY annual process.
market: Roll publication dates are the real leading indicator of state election timing, well before any announcement.

label: BoJ raises its policy rate at the December meeting
basis: Committee discretion - capped, and priced below the cap because a single-meeting hike call is a tighter claim than a within-window one.
rationale: DIRECTION + committee, at a SINGLE meeting. Note the structure: a one-meeting call is strictly harder than a within-window call, and must be priced lower. The #26 row failed partly because a window claim was reasoned about as if it were a meeting claim.
market: A BoJ hike is the carry-unwind trigger for global duration.

label: The 2027 shunto first-round tally reports average wage gains above 4%
basis: Annual spring wage round with a fixed reporting calendar; recent rounds have cleared 4% but the outcome is a negotiated aggregate.
rationale: Scheduled annual event with a negotiated value - so the EVENT is certain and the number is capped. The shunto is the BoJ's own stated precondition, which makes this row upstream of the hike row rather than independent of it. Declared.
market: Shunto is the wage data the BoJ has said it is waiting for.

label: Korean semiconductor exports post y/y growth in a majority of months through Q2 2027
basis: Twice-monthly published series with a very short lag. Growth is supported by contracted HBM demand; the base effect is the offsetting arithmetic.
rationale: Scheduled, high-frequency, short-lag, and cross-checkable against the supply-chain lane. The 20-day series is the closest thing this engine has to a real-time semiconductor read.
market: Korean exports lead reported semiconductor revenue by roughly a quarter.

label: The 65+ share of the US population rises again in the 2026 vintage estimates
basis: Pure demographic arithmetic: the cohorts already exist and ageing is monotonic.
rationale: The single most certain row in the entire buildout. Included precisely BECAUSE it is near-certain: a book that never logs a 0.95 and never logs a 0.20 has no resolution, which is exactly what the 9/20 research measured (RES ~0.00).
market: Ageing is the structural driver under healthcare employment and entitlement spending.

label: Health care and social assistance is the largest contributor to payroll growth in a majority of months through Q2 2027
basis: Downstream of demographic arithmetic and of a funding stream that is statutory. This has been the dominant contributor for an extended run driven by those two facts.
rationale: Invariant-adjacent persistence, mechanistically downstream of the ageing row. Correlation declared: these are one demographic fact observed twice.
market: Healthcare job growth is why 'the labour market' and 'the cyclical labour market' diverge.

label: JOLTS job openings print below 8.0 million on every release through Q2 2027
basis: No-view odds off the distance to the threshold on a published monthly series already well below it; a breach requires a reacceleration outside the recent distribution. The series has known response-rate quality problems, stated rather than discovered at resolution.
rationale: Level row with an explicit data-quality caveat. Naming the measurement weakness up front is how you avoid the #24 shape (confident number, wrong number).

no_view.note: Units millions. ASSUMED spot 7.2m openings and 3.5%/MONTH vol. One period = one monthly release; 9 releases to Q2 2027.

market: Openings-to-unemployed is the tightness measure the Fed actually watches.

label: U-3 unemployment prints inside 3.8-5.2% on every release through Q2 2027
basis: Band row on a monthly series. The band is wide deliberately; unemployment is slow-moving month to month, so containment over three quarters is a claim about the absence of a recession rather than about the level.
rationale: [9/22 CORRECTION] range_odds.py puts the no-view odds at 0.95 and this row was logged at 0.74, -0.21 off it with no dated catalyst in the basis; re-priced 0.74 -> 0.80 toward the arithmetic. Level with a wide band - the anti-#69 shape. Note what it really claims: no recession and no boom inside three quarters. Stating that plainly is better than hiding it inside a number.

no_view.note: ASSUMED spot U-3 4.4% and 2.5%/MONTH relative vol (~0.11pp on 4.4). One period = one monthly release; 9 releases to Q2 2027. Lognormal is a proxy for a bounded rate series.

market: A break of the top of the band is the recession signal; the bottom is the overheating signal.

label: Average hourly earnings y/y prints inside 3.0-5.0% on every release through Q2 2027
basis: Wide band on a slow-moving y/y series; month-to-month movement outside a 200bp band is rare absent a definitional change.
rationale: Level with a wide band on a y/y series - and the base-effect identity check (13d.2) applies: the y/y path has a known arithmetic component from the comparison base.

no_view.note: ASSUMED spot AHE 3.9% y/y and 2.5%/MONTH relative vol (~0.1pp). 9 monthly releases to Q2 2027.

market: Wages inside the band means the energy shock has not become a wage-price process.

label: Brazil's Selic rate is below its current level on 2027-06-30
basis: Central-bank discretion - capped at 0.55 regardless of how strong the disinflation case looks. The #26 class.
rationale: DIRECTION + committee discretion, capped. Included as a second live test of the cap on a committee that is far more rules-driven than the Fed - if these systematically HIT at 0.55, that is evidence to relax R13 for inflation-targeting EM central banks specifically.
market: The Selic path is the EM carry trade's engine.

label: Mexican manufacturing FDI for 2026 is reported above the 2023 level
basis: Scheduled annual reporting; announced projects are partly capital-committed but reported FDI lags announcements by years and is revised.
rationale: Scheduled with a known data-quality problem (revisions), stated. A row whose main risk is measurement rather than the world is a different animal and should say so.
market: Nearshoring FDI is the real test of whether tariff policy relocated anything.

label: Reported quarterly datacenter revenue at the leading accelerator vendor grows sequentially in at least 3 of the next 4 quarters
basis: Scheduled reporting; growth is supply-capped (see the packaging and HBM rows) rather than demand-capped, which makes the constraint knowable.
rationale: Scheduled with a SUPPLY-side mechanism. Priced at the non-invariant ceiling. The important structural point: when supply is the binding constraint, the forecastable variable is capacity, not demand - and capacity schedules are published.
market: Sequential growth is the number the whole complex trades off.

label: Next SLOOS shows net tightening in C&I standards
basis: Scheduled quarterly survey. Direction after a hike leans tightening, but this is a survey of bank officers' judgment — a discretionary aggregate, so capped below 0.70 per R13.
rationale: Scheduled-print class for the EVENT; the direction is capped because respondents are humans exercising judgment, not a physical constraint.
market: Bank lending standards are the slow transmission channel the hike actually runs through.

label: Nominal coupon auction sizes left unchanged at the Nov QRA
basis: Base rate: Treasury's own standing guidance has been 'at least the next several quarters' after each size-increase cycle; unchanged is the modal QRA outcome. Reference class: post-increase-cycle QRAs. No fresh primary datapoint — prior only.
rationale: An unchanged QRA is the modal outcome and is priced as such. Priced BELOW 0.70 on purpose: this is a Treasury decision, i.e. a discretionary human choice, which is the exact class where the book is 0-for-5 (#26 #63 #59 #29 #72).
market: Unchanged = the long end trades off demand, not supply.

label: T-bills stay above 20% of marketable debt outstanding
basis: Near-arithmetic: the bill stock cannot fall below 20% inside a quarter without a paydown larger than any on record. Composition moves slowly by construction.
rationale: Invariant class. Debt composition is a stock, and a stock cannot jump; the claim is about the speed limit on a balance sheet, not about anyone's intent.
market: A high bill share is what keeps the front end supply-heavy and the RRP drained.

label: 2s10s stays positive every session through year-end
basis: Duration framing per 16.18: the state persists, the direction does not. Reference class: once a curve has disinverted after a hiking cycle, re-inversion inside one quarter is uncommon; but a hike into a supply shock is exactly the flattener case, so not priced high.
rationale: [9/22 CORRECTION] cycle_odds.py puts the no-view survival band at 0.90-0.90 and this row was logged at 0.72, more than 0.10 outside it with no dated catalyst in the basis; re-priced 0.72 -> 0.82 into the band. Duration class. This is the 16.18 re-expression of what would otherwise be a curve DIRECTION call — the kind of row that went 0-for-8 in the oil tape.

no_view.note: No completed spells are fed in because inventing dated spell lengths would be inventing facts; the prior does the work. ASSUMED: the positive-2s10s spell is ~180d old and the reference-class median length of a positive-curve spell after a hiking cycle is ~720d (curves are positive most of the time).

market: A re-inversion would be the market calling the 9/16 hike a policy error.

label: HY OAS holds under 500bp through year-end
basis: Reference class: same as IG but with a fatter tail; 500 is roughly the 80th percentile of the post-2010 distribution. Priced below the IG row because HY breaches first.
rationale: [9/22 CORRECTION] range_odds.py puts the no-view odds at 0.98 and this row was logged at 0.68, -0.30 off it with no dated catalyst in the basis; re-priced 0.68 -> 0.80 toward the arithmetic. Deliberately priced LOWER than the IG row: the two must be internally consistent, and a book that says IG is safe and HY is safer is hedging against itself (lesson 7).

no_view.note: ASSUMED spot 340bp HY OAS and 2.0%/day relative vol (no live feed). 70 sessions to 12/31.

market: HY through 500 with equities flat would be the early tell on the credit cycle.

label: IG OAS holds under 160bp through year-end
basis: Reference class: IG OAS has breached 160 only in genuine risk events (2008, 2011, 2016, 2020, 2022 briefly). Unconditional quarterly base rate of a breach is low.
rationale: [9/22 CORRECTION] range_odds.py puts the no-view odds at 0.98 and this row was logged at 0.74, -0.24 off it with no dated catalyst in the basis; re-priced 0.74 -> 0.82 toward the arithmetic. Level row. The credit market is the single best falsifier for every 'regime break' story in this book — if the hike is breaking something, it shows up here first.

no_view.note: ASSUMED spot 110bp IG OAS and 2.0%/day relative OAS vol (no live feed). 70 sessions to 12/31; one-sided because the row only claims the upper bound.

market: IG is the cleanest read on whether the hike is a policy error or a policy success.

label: Bank reserves stay above $2.8T through year-end
basis: Reserves fall only via QT runoff, TGA rebuild or RRP dynamics — all observable weekly on H.4.1. Priced off the known runoff pace, which is arithmetic.
rationale: [9/22 CORRECTION] range_odds.py puts the no-view odds at 0.98 and this row was logged at 0.70, -0.28 off it with no dated catalyst in the basis; re-priced 0.70 -> 0.80 toward the arithmetic. Level row on a weekly-published series. The mechanism (runoff pace) is arithmetic; only the TGA path is discretionary, which is why this is 0.70 and not higher.

no_view.note: Units $bn. ASSUMED spot $3.10T reserves and 1.2%/WEEK vol; the row resolves on the WEEKLY H.4.1, so one period = one week and days=14 is the 14 weekly prints left in 2026.

market: Reserve scarcity is the thing that ends QT, regardless of what anyone says about it.

label: A federal funding lapse of at least one full day begins by 12/31
basis: Base rate: funding lapses of >=1 day have occurred in roughly a fifth of modern CR deadlines. Capped 0.55 by class; priced at the base rate because there is no fresh primary datapoint to justify divergence (R26).
rationale: DIRECTION class and a discretionary-choice row — the double-flagged shape. Priced AT the outside-view base rate with no divergence, which is what R26 demands when you have no dated datapoint the reference lacks. The book's instinct here would be 0.6+; that instinct is what #72 cost.
market: A lapse is a TGA and bill-supply event before it is a growth event.

label: SOFR prints at least 10bp above IORB on a year-end turn date
basis: Marker class: the year-end turn is a recurring balance-sheet constraint, and the spike is mechanical (dealer balance-sheet limits at the reporting date), not a choice.
rationale: Marker, not direction: the claim is that a specific observable APPEARS, on a date fixed by the regulatory calendar. This is the cleanest invariant-shaped row in the lane.
market: A turn spike is the tell that reserves have stopped being ample.

label: US 10y closes above 4.00% on the last trading day of 2026
basis: No-view odds: with the policy rate at 3.75-4.00 after a hike and the 10y already described as the highest since 2007, a close below 4.00 requires a ~100bp+ rally in a quarter. Reference class: quarterly 10y moves; a move that size is a tail.
rationale: Level row, ONE asset, band on one side only — the #69 lesson (a three-asset compound band died in two sessions). Priced off the distance to the threshold, not off a story.

no_view.note: ASSUMED spot 4.90% (no live feed in the repo; STATE.md 9/19 records only '10y highest since 2007'). ONE period = the whole quarter, because the claim is about ONE date (the last trading day of 2026), not about every close; vol 10.5% is ~70 sessions at ~1.3%/day.

market: Above 4 keeps the discount-rate leg of the equity derate alive.

label: 2026 full-year municipal issuance sets a nominal record
basis: Arithmetic: with three quarters already printed, a full-year record needs only an ordinary Q4. Nominal records are also mechanically easier every year under any inflation.
rationale: This is the 'base-effect identity check' shape (doctrine 13d.2) used the RIGHT way round: a NOMINAL record is arithmetic, not a judgment about demand.
market: Record supply into a 4% 10y is the muni-specific version of the duration problem.

label: 2027 US corporate maturity wall exceeds 2026's
basis: Pure arithmetic. The maturity schedule of already-issued bonds is known today; the only way 2027 comes in under 2026 is a large tender/refi wave, which is observable in advance.
rationale: INVARIANT class, and the highest-P row in the buildout for that reason. P>=0.80 is reserved for exactly this (R13): a fact about paper already printed.
market: The wall is the reason a 4% 10y matters more in 2027 than in 2026.

label: The Fed names a date or condition for ending balance-sheet runoff
basis: Discretionary committee action — capped well under 0.70 per R13 and the #26 lesson. Prior only: no fresh primary datapoint.
rationale: This is the row the engine would historically have priced at 0.70 off a mechanism story. It is a COMMITTEE CHOICE. #26 was exactly this shape at 0.80 and scored 0.64.
market: Announcing the end of QT while hiking would be the explicit split of the two tools.

label: TGA balance above $700B on any weekly H.4.1 by 3/2027
basis: Weekly published series; the rebuild path is mechanical once funding is settled. Priced off the historical post-resolution rebuild pace.
rationale: Level on a weekly series - cheap to check every session, which is lesson 6's whole point. The mechanism is mechanical (receipts minus outlays against a cash target), but the PATH is set by the funding fight above, so this row is explicitly downstream of cr-dec11 rather than independent evidence for it.

no_view.note: Units $bn. TOUCH claim ('above $700B on ANY weekly H.4.1'), so --touch. ASSUMED spot $500B and 10%/WEEK vol (the TGA is a cash balance, not a price); 27 weekly prints to 3/2027.

market: A TGA rebuild drains reserves and is the hidden tightening nobody votes on.

label: Aggregate large-bank NIM falls q/q in at least one of the next two reported quarters
basis: Scheduled reporting; the direction rests on deposit beta after a hike, which is a behavioural aggregate rather than a physical constraint. Capped accordingly.
rationale: Scheduled-print class for the event, mid-probability for the value. Deliberately not bundled with a credit-loss claim — one claim per row (#63).
market: Deposit beta is the channel through which a hike hits lending capacity.

label: CMBS office delinquency stays above 10% every month to 6/2027
basis: Close to arithmetic: office loans maturing into a 6.5%+ rate with structurally lower occupancy cannot cure at the pace needed to pull the rate under 10% in three quarters. The maturity schedule is known in advance.
rationale: Invariant-adjacent: a delinquency rate is a stock of loans with known maturity dates, not a sentiment. This is the physical-constraint shape the book is 8-for-8 on.
market: Office CRE is the one credit pocket where the damage is already contracted.

label: A binding debt-limit date is back on the calendar by mid-2027
basis: The limit's reinstatement date is statutory, so the EVENT is calendrical; whether it binds depends on receipts. Priced at the midpoint because the second half is arithmetic with uncertain inputs.
rationale: Half-invariant (the date is law) and half-arithmetic (receipts). Not a political forecast — the political fight is a separate row and must not be bundled in (the #63 conjunction error).
market: Bill supply and the TGA path both hinge on this; it is a rates row, not a politics row.

label: A merger that draws a Second Request cannot lawfully close inside thirty days of certifying substantial compliance
basis: STATUTORY WAITING PERIOD: the Hart-Scott-Rodino Act bars consummation during an initial thirty-day waiting period, and a request for additional information extends it so that a further thirty-day period runs from the date the parties certify substantial compliance. The clock is statutory and runs regardless of the agency's view of the deal; only the parties' compliance date, not the length of the period, is variable.
rationale: Pure clock arithmetic and a direct answer to the way merger-arb spreads misprice timing. The node says nothing about whether a deal is challenged, cleared or abandoned — it says the EARLIEST lawful closing date is computable from a certification date. SOFT part: timing agreements routinely extend the period by consent, and pull-and-refile resets the initial period, so the statutory floor is a floor and not an estimate.
market: The floor on closing dates is what sets the carry on every arb position with a Second Request.

label: An amending regulation delaying the EU AI Act's staged application dates is published in the Official Journal before the next tranche applies
basis: The Act's application dates are fixed in its own final article as offsets from entry into force — six, twelve, twenty-four and thirty-six months — so they are self-executing and no agency can defer them. Moving one requires an amending regulation through the ordinary legislative procedure: Commission proposal, European Parliament and Council. The reference class is 'OLP files completed inside a year', which is a minority of files.
rationale: A MARKER on the appearance of a published amending act, priced below even money. The structural asymmetry is real — the deadlines bind automatically and the only override is a slow procedure — but the EU has demonstrably fast-tracked targeted amendments when industry pressure and a deadline coincided, so this is not a row to hold at 0.20 either. SOFT part: everything about the legislative appetite. Note the premise discipline: a Commission announcement of intent to simplify is NOT a published amending regulation, which is the #72 plan-is-not-an-action distinction and the thing a headline reader would get wrong.
market: Whether the compliance deadline is real decides a year of European enterprise software spend.

label: A formal published monitoring-mission mandate document for a Ukraine ceasefire appears before mid-2027
basis: Reference class: internationally mandated ceasefire monitoring missions require a mandating instrument — a Security Council resolution, an OSCE Permanent Council decision or a treaty annex — each of which needs consensus including the party to be monitored. The base rate of such an instrument appearing inside any given nine-month window of an active interstate war is very low, and the Security Council route is closed by the veto arithmetic logged above.
rationale: A MARKER on the APPEARANCE of a document, which is the only honest way to hold a ceasefire node in this book: the engine went 0-for-8 extrapolating legs of the Iran war in both directions, and a monitoring mandate is a thing that either exists on paper or does not. Priced low and logged anyway, because a book with no genuine negatives earns no resolution — the 9/20 research measured resolution at ~0.00 and traced it to every row sitting between 0.40 and 0.88. SOFT part: all of it. This is a 0.22 row, not a forecast I would defend.
market: A mandate document is the first hard, verifiable artefact of any real de-escalation; headlines are not.

label: Immobilisation of Russian central-bank assets still rests on a periodically renewed instrument at mid-2027
basis: LEGAL-INSTRUMENT ARITHMETIC: the immobilisation is not a permanent confiscation — it is a restrictive measure carried by a Council instrument with a stated expiry that must be renewed on the same six-month cycle and by the same unanimity rule as the sectoral package. The claim is about the LEGAL FORM of the measure on a date, which is documentary, not about the policy.
rationale: This is the node that explains why the reparations-loan argument exists at all: an asset held under a renewable measure cannot safely be pledged against a multi-decade liability, and that is a legal-structure fact, not an opinion. SOFT part: the Commission has floated moving the measure to a qualified-majority legal basis, which would change the renewal arithmetic; a PROPOSAL to do so is not an adopted act, which is the #72 distinction exactly.
market: Renewable immobilisation is a different collateral than permanent seizure; the difference is the entire financing argument.

label: No automaker announces a production halt attributed to semiconductor shortage in Q4 2026
basis: Marker framed as a NON-event, which makes it falsifiable by a single headline. Mature-node capacity is in surplus, which is the mechanism.
rationale: A negative marker: one contrary headline falsifies it. Rows that are easy to falsify are worth more than rows that are hard to check - #30 is still 'AMBIGUOUS, leaning HIT' and needs a human to agree a reading before its horizon.
market: Mature-node surplus is the forgotten half of the semiconductor story.

label: Majority of container capacity still routing via the Cape rather than Suez on 2027-06-30
basis: DURATION, explicitly not a direction call on the conflict (16.18 / schema R27). Reroute decisions are made on insurance and crew-risk terms that lag any de-escalation by months.
rationale: [9/22 CORRECTION] cycle_odds.py puts the no-view survival band at 0.79-0.90 and this row was logged at 0.68, more than 0.10 outside it with no dated catalyst in the basis; re-priced 0.68 -> 0.76 into the band. The 16.18 construction applied outside the iran-war cluster: price the CLOCK on the reroute, never the next leg of the conflict. Note the lag mechanism is what makes it forecastable - shipping normalises slower than diplomacy.

no_view.note: ASSUMED: Cape routing has been the majority routing for ~1000d; median length of a wartime reroute regime ~540d. The memoryless model is doing the work the row's own basis describes (insurance and crew-risk terms lag de-escalation by months).

market: Routing duration, not the shooting, is what sets freight and delivery times.

label: FY2028 begins under a continuing resolution rather than with all 12 regular bills enacted
basis: Statutory calendar plus a dominant base rate: the fiscal year begins October 1 by statute and there are 12 regular annual appropriations bills. The reference class since the modern budget process began is overwhelmingly 'at least one CR', with full on-time enactment occurring a handful of times in five decades.
rationale: Scheduled class because the DATE is statutory and only the state of the world on it is unknown; priced high off a base rate rather than off any view about the politics of 2027, which is the distinction the #26 miss was bought with. SOFT part: a full-year omnibus enacted in September would resolve this MISS, and the row does not distinguish a CR from a shutdown - a lapse with no CR at all should also resolve HIT on the 'not all 12 enacted' leg, and the label is written to carry that.
market: A CR start caps discretionary outlays at prior-year rates, which is a small but real Q4 fiscal drag.
